title: Give creators something precise to point to.
intro: The next challenge was the handoff between natural language and direct manipulation. “Move that a little later” only becomes useful when the product knows what “that” refers to.

I designed selection and reference as part of the editing workflow. A scene object, character path, camera or shot could provide the scope for the next Agent request, while remaining available for manual adjustment.

blocks.alt: A purple continuous character path in the 3D scene paired with path keyframes below
blocks.caption: Delivered product · Selecting a character path opens its focused timeline. The spatial route and timed keyframes describe the same movement.

items.title: Where?
body: Select a point directly on the path to understand and adjust its position in the scene.

items.title: When?
body: The corresponding timeline point places that moment within the movement.

items.title: What does the camera see?
body: The monitor connects an edit in space and time to the resulting composition.

blocks.label: THE HUMAN–AGENT LOOP
blocks.text: AI drafts → the creator refines → AI revises a defined part.

body: I favored meaningful subjects over raw geometry in reference lists: a whole building or Ferris wheel first, with precise parts available through direct selection. This gave creators a useful level of control without making them navigate every generated primitive.

With the two engineers focused on Agent capabilities, I translated this into handoff requirements: explicit targets, current editing context, revision protection and undo. A request needed to act on the current scene and respect the scope the creator had chosen.
